## spec:shadow
================================================================================

I now have all the information needed. The Metal shader side (`sun_shadow.h` with the extended parameter signature, `deferred_pbr.metal` wiring) is already ported. The spec must cover the CPU-side Metal driver work: creating the depth atlas, the shadow render pass, depth-only pipelines, sun-frustum fitting, the compare sampler, and binding into deferred lighting. I have enough to write the detailed spec.

Metal shadow pass specification for the native `GEMetalDriver`.

---

# Metal Sun-Shadow Pass Specification

## 0. Scope and current state

The Metal **shader side is already ported**: `data/shaders/ge_metal/common/sun_shadow.h` (numerically identical PCF+PCSS, 2-cascade 2×1 atlas) and `data/shaders/ge_metal/deferred_pbr.metal` (which calls `getSunShadowFactor(...)` and declares `depth2d<float> u_sun_shadow_pcf` + a compare `sampler` at local texture/sampler slot 3, and `texture2d<float> u_sun_shadow_raw` + linear `sampler` at slot 4). The `GECameraBuffer` MSL struct in `data/shaders/ge_metal/shared/ge_metal_bindings.h` already carries `m_sun_shadow_matrix`, `m_shadow_params`, `m_sun_shadow_matrix_far`, `m_shadow_params_far` in the same layout as the Vulkan UBO.

Therefore **everything remaining is CPU-side, in `lib/graphics_engine/src/ge_metal_driver.mm`**: allocate the depth atlas, build depth-only pipelines and a shadow render pass, fit the two sun frusta each frame, populate the camera buffer's shadow fields, render the atlas, and bind the two texture views + two samplers into the deferred-lighting encoder. Note that the Metal backend is currently a **forward renderer with no G-buffer / deferred pass yet** (commit log ends at "skybox + standard-vertex 3D geometry path"). The deferred lighting pass that consumes the shadow map does not yet exist on the Metal side; this spec assumes it is being built alongside, and the shadow pass plugs into it exactly where `deferred_pbr.metal` reads slots 3/4. Until the deferred composite exists, the shadow atlas can be produced and validated in isolation (e.g. blitted to screen).

The single hard requirement is **numerical parity** with Vulkan: the Metal atlas layout, projection z-range convention, UV-bias matrix, texel/penumbra params, and depth-compare semantics must match `sun_shadow.h` bit-for-bit, because that shader is a verbatim port. Any deviation shows up as shadow acne, peter-panning, or a cascade seam.

Reference implementation: `GEVulkanDrawCall::createShadowResources / createShadowPipelines / updateSunShadowCamera / renderShadowMap / getShadowCameraOffset` in `lib/graphics_engine/src/ge_vulkan_draw_call.cpp`, sampler `GVS_SHADOW` in `ge_vulkan_driver.cpp:1580-1593`.

---

## 1. Depth-only shadow render target (the atlas)

**One depth texture, a 2×1 atlas.** Near cascade in the left half, far cascade in the right half. Do **not** use a texture array or two separate textures — the shader's UV-bias matrix bakes in `u_base = 0.0 / 0.5` and scales horizontal offsets by `0.5` (`const vec2 AXIS = vec2(0.5, 1.0)` in the GLSL), so both cascades must live side-by-side in a single texture whose width is twice its height.

- `size = clamp(getGEConfig()->m_shadow_map_size, 256, 4096)`, default `512` if `<= 0` (matches Vulkan `createShadowResources`). Atlas dimensions are `(size*2, size)`.
- `MTLTextureDescriptor` with:
  - `pixelFormat = MTLPixelFormatDepth32Float`. This matches the Vulkan depth attachment format used for the map and the `depth2d<float>` the MSL shader binds. Do not use a combined depth/stencil format — the Vulkan render pass uses `DONT_CARE` stencil and no stencil is sampled.
  - `usage = MTLTextureUsageRenderTarget | MTLTextureUsageShaderRead`. Both are required: written as a depth attachment in the shadow pass, read as `depth2d`/`texture2d` in the deferred pass. This is the Metal analogue of the Vulkan image being both a depth attachment and `SAMPLED`.
  - `storageMode = MTLStorageModePrivate` (GPU-only; never CPU-mapped).
  - `width = size*2, height = size, mipmapped = NO`.
- The texture is a **persistent, driver-owned resource**, allocated once when the deferred FBO / PBR path is created (mirroring `createShadowResources`, which is gated on `getGEConfig()->m_pbr` and a deferred RTT). Recreate only on shadow-map-size change or device loss. On Apple GPUs this is a normal private texture; there is no "lazy/transient memoryless" benefit because it is read in a later pass (it must survive to the deferred encoder).

**Two texture handles for the same texture.** The deferred shader binds the atlas twice — once as `depth2d<float>` (PCF slot 3) and once as `texture2d<float>` (raw slot 4). In Metal you can bind the *same* `id<MTLTexture>` to both a `depth2d` and a `texture2d` fragment argument; a `Depth32Float` texture is legal to read through either declaration. No second texture and no `newTextureViewWithPixelFormat:` is required — bind the one atlas texture to both `setFragmentTexture:atIndex:3` and `:atIndex:4`. The distinction between "compare" and "raw" sampling is entirely in the two *samplers* (Section 3), not the texture.

**First-frame safety.** Vulkan pre-transitions the image to `DEPTH_STENCIL_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL` so the very first deferred pass can sample it even before the shadow pass runs. Metal has automatic hazard tracking, so no explicit barrier is needed, but the atlas must still contain valid depth on frame 0. Either (a) always run the shadow pass before the deferred pass every frame (preferred — the shader reads garbage-safe values of 1.0 = "lit" for untouched texels because the clear is 1.0), or (b) if shadows are disabled, clear the atlas to 1.0 once. The shader's `m_shadow_params.x <= 0.0` early-out (Section 5) makes an un-rendered atlas harmless regardless.

---

## 2. Shadow render pass and depth-only pipelines

### 2.1 Render pass descriptor

The shadow pass is a **depth-only pass — zero color attachments**. Build one `MTLRenderPassDescriptor` per shadow render:

- `depthAttachment.texture = shadowAtlas`
- `depthAttachment.loadAction = MTLLoadActionClear`
- `depthAttachment.clearDepth = 1.0` (matches Vulkan `clear_value.depthStencil = {1.0, 0}`)
- `depthAttachment.storeAction = MTLStoreActionStore` (must persist to the deferred pass)
- `colorAttachments[0].texture = nil` — no color. In Metal a render encoder with no color attachments is valid provided a depth attachment (and, for tile size inference, `renderTargetWidth/Height`) is set. Set `rp.renderTargetWidth = size*2`, `rp.renderTargetHeight = size` explicitly since there is no color attachment to infer dimensions from.

**Both cascades render into this single pass/encoder**, distinguished by viewport + scissor (Section 4), exactly like `renderShadowMap` which begins one render pass then loops `c = 0,1` setting viewport/scissor to the left/right half. Do **not** open two render passes — a second `LoadActionClear` would wipe the first cascade. Use one encoder, one clear, two viewport rectangles.

### 2.2 Depth-only render pipeline state

Mirror `createShadowPipelines`. For every solid (non-transparent) material that has a depth-only fragment shader, build an `MTLRenderPipelineState`:

- **Vertex function**: the material's depth/prepass vertex function (the same vertex shader used by the Metal depth-prepass, static and skinning variants — build both where a skinning vertex shader exists).
- **Fragment function**: `depth_only_main` from `data/shaders/ge_metal/depth_only.metal` — an empty fragment that writes no color. (Alpha-tested materials that need a discard in the shadow pass would use their alphatest depth variant, matching the Vulkan `m_depth_only_fragment_shader` selection; the current Metal `depth_only.metal` is the pure no-op case.)
- `pipelineDescriptor.colorAttachments[0].pixelFormat = MTLPixelFormatInvalid` (no color).
- `pipelineDescriptor.depthAttachmentPixelFormat = MTLPixelFormatDepth32Float`.
- `rasterSampleCount = 1` (the atlas is single-sampled).
- Vertex descriptor identical to the main mesh pipelines (the shadow pass reuses the standard vertex layout — Vulkan uses `getDefaultVertexDescription()`).

### 2.3 Depth-stencil state

One `MTLDepthStencilState`:
- `depthCompareFunction = MTLCompareFunctionLess` (matches Vulkan `VK_COMPARE_OP_LESS`).
- `depthWriteEnabled = YES`.
- No stencil.

### 2.4 Rasterizer / bias state (set on the encoder, not the PSO)

Metal puts depth bias and winding/cull on the *encoder*, not the pipeline:

- **Depth bias — critical for parity.** Vulkan sets `depthBiasConstantFactor = 2.0`, `depthBiasSlopeFactor = 4.0`, `depthBiasClamp = 0`. The Metal call is `[enc setDepthBias:2.0 slopeScale:4.0 clamp:0.0]`. These constants pair with the shader-side normal-offset and receiver-depth biases in `sun_shadow.h`; changing them re-introduces acne or peter-panning. Keep `2.0 / 4.0`.

  Caveat: Vulkan's constant factor is scaled by the depth format's minimum representable value (r), and for `Depth32Float` that scaling is implementation-defined but effectively `r ≈ 2^-23`-ish per unit; Metal's `setDepthBias` constant is in the same "format-relative units" as Vulkan's constant factor for float depth. In practice `2.0` transfers directly. If a fine acne/peter-pan difference appears versus Vulkan on the same scene, this is the first knob to nudge — but start at `2.0 / 4.0`.

- **Front face**: `[enc setFrontFacingWinding:MTLWindingClockwise]` — Vulkan uses `VK_FRONT_FACE_CLOCKWISE`, and commit `a4dcc2f` already established CW-front for the Metal 3D path.
- **Cull mode**: per-material — `MTLCullModeBack` when `m_backface_culling`, else `MTLCullModeNone` (matches the per-material `cullMode` in `createShadowPipelines`). Rendering back faces (or front, depending on the caster) is a common shadow-acne mitigation; here parity means *matching Vulkan's per-material choice*, not switching to front-face culling.

---

## 3. The comparison sampler (and the raw sampler)

Two `MTLSamplerState` objects, bound to the deferred encoder at sampler indices 3 (PCF/compare) and 4 (raw), matching `deferred_pbr.metal`.

### 3.1 PCF compare sampler (slot 3) — `depth2d.sample_compare`

This is the Metal equivalent of Vulkan's `GVS_SHADOW` (`ge_vulkan_driver.cpp:1580-1593`), which sets `compareEnable = TRUE`, `compareOp = VK_COMPARE_OP_LESS_OR_EQUAL`, `LINEAR` min/mag, `CLAMP_TO_EDGE` on all axes.

`MTLSamplerDescriptor`:
- `compareFunction = MTLCompareFunctionLessEqual` — **exactly** matches `VK_COMPARE_OP_LESS_OR_EQUAL`. This is what makes `depth2d.sample_compare(s, uv, ref)` return the fraction of the 2×2 (bilinear PCF) tap where `stored_depth >= ref` (i.e. the receiver at `ref` is *not* occluded). The shader's `sampleSunShadowCascade` relies on this hardware 2×2 comparison per tap ("3x3 with hardware 2x2 per tap").
- `minFilter = MTLSamplerMinMagFilterLinear`, `magFilter = MTLSamplerMinMagFilterLinear` — linear filtering is what turns the compare into hardware bilinear PCF. Do **not** set nearest here.
- `mipFilter = MTLSamplerMipFilterNotMipmapped` (the atlas has no mips).
- `sAddressMode = tAddressMode = rAddressMode = MTLSamplerAddressModeClampToEdge`.
- `normalizedCoordinates = YES`.

**`supportArgumentBuffers` / access from fragment.** A compare sampler is a normal fragment sampler in Metal; nothing special beyond `compareFunction`. The compare is invoked by the shader via `.sample_compare`, which the ported `sun_shadow.h` already does (its `sample2DShadow`-equivalent path). No shader change needed.

**Important MSL constraint the shader already respects:** `sample_compare` requires the compare `sampler` be declared with a compile-time `compare_func` in some MSL versions, but the runtime `MTLSamplerState.compareFunction` is the canonical path used here and by the existing `deferred_pbr.metal`. The reference value `ref_z` passed to `sample_compare` is already in [0,1] because the CPU bakes the z-remap into `m_sun_shadow_matrix` (see Section 4 / the header comment "the CPU bakes the remap into m_sun_shadow_matrix").

### 3.2 Raw depth sampler (slot 4) — `texture2d.sample(...).x`

Used by the **PCSS blocker search** (`if (z_occ < ref_z)`), which reads unfiltered occluder depths and averages them itself. This corresponds to Vulkan binding the same shadow image with `vk->getSampler(GVS_NEAREST)` at descriptor binding 6 (`ge_vulkan_draw_call.cpp:3093-3094`).

`MTLSamplerDescriptor`:
- **No `compareFunction`** (leave default `MTLCompareFunctionNever`) — this sampler must return the *stored depth value*, not a comparison result.
- `minFilter = magFilter = MTLSamplerMinMagFilterNearest` — the GLSL uses `texture(u_sun_shadow_raw, tc).x` for the blocker search and reads individual texel depths; `GVS_NEAREST` is nearest. Match it with nearest (linear would blur blocker depths and skew the penumbra estimate).
- `mipFilter = NotMipmapped`.
- All address modes `ClampToEdge`, `normalizedCoordinates = YES`.

Both samplers are static, created once at driver init alongside the other `GEMetalDriver` samplers.

---

## 4. Per-frame sun-frustum fitting and camera-buffer population

Port `updateSunShadowCamera` (`ge_vulkan_draw_call.cpp:1618-1789`) essentially verbatim into the Metal path. This is pure CPU math (Irrlicht `matrix4`), **backend-independent except for the clip-space convention** — and Vulkan and Metal share the same [0,1] NDC-z and top-left origin, so the math transfers unchanged. Key points to preserve exactly:

- **Constants**: `SPLIT = 16.0`, `SHADOW_RANGE = 60.0`, `CASTER_MARGIN = 150.0`, sun-position push-back `sun_dir * 200.0`, far-plane pad `+10.0`. These define the split boundary that the shader blends across (`m_shadow_params_far.y` = `SPLIT`, blend starts at `SPLIT*0.8`).
- **Two cascades** with overlapping z-ranges: near `[near, 16]`, far `[12, min(60, farValue)]`. The overlap is deliberate so the shader's cross-split blend never samples outside a cascade.
- **Frustum corner extraction** from the *unwarped* player view/projection (relativity warp is excluded — the atlas is rendered from unwarped world positions; see the `sun_shadow.glsl` comment on `rel_fade`).
- **Texel snapping** (anti-shimmer): `cx = floor(cx/texel_x)*texel_x`, same for y, with `texel = w/res`, `res = size` (the per-cascade square height).
- **Off-centre orthographic matrix built straight into [0,1] clip-z**: the Vulkan code hand-builds `ortho` with `o[10] = 1/(zf-zn)`, `o[14] = -zn/(zf-zn)` — i.e. depth mapped to [0,1], not [-1,1]. **This is exactly the Metal convention**, so copy it verbatim. Do not apply any GL-style [-1,1] z remap.
- **UV-bias matrix** (world → atlas UV + depth01), verbatim:
  - `b[0] = 0.25` (x scale: 0.5 for NDC→UV × 0.5 for half-atlas width)
  - `b[5] = 0.5` (y scale: NDC→UV)
  - `b[10] = 1.0` (z passes through — already [0,1])
  - `b[12] = 0.25 + 0.5*c` (x offset: 0.25 for near half-centre, 0.75 for far half)
  - `b[13] = 0.5` (y offset)
  - `sample_matrix[c] = uv_bias * sun_pv`
  
  **Metal note on the V axis:** Vulkan and Metal both use a top-left texture origin, and this bias matrix produces `v` with the standard orientation the shader expects. Because the *same* matrix is consumed by the *same* ported shader math and the atlas is rendered with the same clip-space y as the deferred pass reads it, no V-flip is needed. (If the Metal viewport/blit for the atlas ends up y-flipped relative to Vulkan, the fix belongs in the viewport, not this matrix — but with a standard `MTLViewport` and the same ortho matrix, it matches.)
- **Params packing** (`m_shadow_params` / `m_shadow_params_far`), verbatim:
  - `[0]` = `zf - zn` (depth range in world metres; `0` means shadows off — the shader early-outs on `<= 0`)
  - `[1]` = near: PCSS flag (`m_pcss ? 1 : 0`); far: `SPLIT` (the split distance the shader reads as `m_shadow_params_far.y`)
  - `[2]` = `1.0 / res` (texel size in atlas-UV, v axis)
  - `[3]` = `0.02 / w` (penumbra UV radius per metre of receiver–blocker separation)

- **Write into the camera buffer.** The Metal path uploads one `GECameraBuffer` (the player camera) that the deferred pass reads. Populate `m_sun_shadow_matrix`, `m_shadow_params`, `m_sun_shadow_matrix_far`, `m_shadow_params_far` on it — the same four fields `setSunShadowData` writes on the Vulkan camera UBO (`ge_vulkan_camera_scene_node.hpp:141-149`). Irrlicht `matrix4` is column-vector-major and maps directly to `float4x4`; upload the raw 16 floats.

- **The two shadow *render* cameras.** Vulkan appends two extra camera UBOs (`m_shadow_camera_ubo[0/1]`) after the player camera in one buffer, bound during the shadow pass via a dynamic offset (`getShadowCameraOffset(cascade)`), so the depth-only vertex shader transforms geometry by the sun's `projection_view_matrix`. In Metal, the equivalent is: build two small camera buffers (or two regions of one buffer) each holding the sun `light_view` / `ortho` / `sun_pv` matrices (relativity blocks zeroed, `m_relativity_bubble` pushed to `1e8` so adaptive tessellation collapses to level 1 — same as Vulkan), and bind the matching one to the vertex stage at `buffer(GE_MTL_BUF_CAMERA=0)` before rendering each cascade. The depth-only vertex function reuses the standard camera-buffer layout, so these are just `GECameraBuffer` instances with only the matrix fields meaningful.

---

## 5. Rendering the atlas each frame

Port `renderShadowMap`:

1. Skip entirely if shadows disabled (`m_shadow_map_size <= 0`) or no draw commands. (The player camera's `m_shadow_params.x` will be `0`, so the deferred shader early-outs and returns `1.0` = fully lit — the atlas contents are then irrelevant.)
2. Open the depth-only render encoder (Section 2.1), one clear to depth 1.0.
3. `setFrontFacingWinding:MTLWindingClockwise`, `setDepthStencilState:` the Less/write state, `setDepthBias:2.0 slopeScale:4.0 clamp:0.0`.
4. **For each cascade `c = 0, 1`:**
   - `MTLViewport vp = { originX = c*size, originY = 0, width = size, height = size, znear = 0, zfar = 1 }` → `[enc setViewport:vp]`. (Left half for near, right half for far — matches `vp.x = c*res`.)
   - `MTLScissorRect sc = { x = c*size, y = 0, width = size, height = size }` → `[enc setScissor:sc]`.
   - Bind cascade `c`'s sun camera buffer to `buffer(0)` (vertex).
   - Draw all solid caster geometry with the depth-only pipelines: for each material batch set its depth-only PSO, per-material `setCullMode:`, bind vertex/index buffers and per-object data exactly as the main forward pass does, and `drawIndexedPrimitives`.
5. `endEncoding`.

This encoder must be submitted **before** the deferred lighting encoder in the same command buffer. Metal's automatic hazard tracking inserts the write-shadow→read-shadow dependency (the analogue of the Vulkan subpass dependencies at `ge_vulkan_draw_call.cpp:1201-1215`); no manual barrier/fence is required within one command buffer. If the shadow pass and deferred pass are ever split across command buffers, add an `MTLFence` or rely on same-queue serialization.

---

## 6. How deferred lighting reads the shadow map

The consumer is `data/shaders/ge_metal/deferred_pbr.metal`, already written. On the CPU, when recording the deferred fullscreen lighting draw, the driver must bind, on the **fragment** stage of the deferred encoder:

- `setFragmentTexture:shadowAtlas atIndex:3` — read as `depth2d<float> u_sun_shadow_pcf`.
- `setFragmentSamplerState:shadowCompareSampler atIndex:3` — the LessEqual compare sampler (Section 3.1).
- `setFragmentTexture:shadowAtlas atIndex:4` — the **same** atlas texture, read as `texture2d<float> u_sun_shadow_raw`.
- `setFragmentSamplerState:shadowRawSampler atIndex:4` — the nearest, no-compare sampler (Section 3.2).
- `setFragmentBuffer:playerCameraBuffer atIndex:GE_MTL_BUF_CAMERA(0)` — carrying the four shadow fields from Section 4.
- `setFragmentBuffer:globalLightBuffer atIndex:GE_MTL_BUF_GLOBAL_LIGHT(3)` — for `m_sun_direction`.

The shader then, per fragment: reconstructs `world_pos` from the G-buffer depth + `m_inverse_view_matrix`, derives a derivative-based `geo_normal` for slope-scaled bias, selects/blends cascades by view-space `xpos.z` against `m_shadow_params_far.y` (=`SPLIT`) with blend start at `0.8*SPLIT`, transforms `world_pos` by `m_sun_shadow_matrix` / `_far` to atlas UV+depth, and runs either 3×3 hardware-PCF (`sample_compare`) or PCSS (8-tap blocker search via the raw sampler, then 16-tap Vogel PCF via the compare sampler). It returns a `[0,1]` sun-visibility factor fed into `handlePBRDeferred`. Relativity fade (`rel_fade` on observer beta) and the back-facing early-out are all inside the ported shader — no CPU involvement.

Because the shadow slots (3/4) are **local per-pass texture/sampler indices** used only by `deferred_pbr.metal` (they do not collide with the G-buffer at 0/1/2, AO at 7, or IBL at 8/9 — see the slot map in `deferred_pbr.metal:63-69`), the driver only needs to bind them when recording that one fullscreen draw. No global argument-buffer or descriptor-set churn.

---

## 7. Parity checklist (things that will silently break the port if changed)

1. Atlas is **one** `Depth32Float` texture, `2*size × size`, near left / far right — not an array, not two textures.
2. Ortho projection maps depth to **[0,1]** (`o[10]=1/(zf-zn)`), no GL [-1,1] remap.
3. UV-bias matrix constants `0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0` and x-offset `0.25 + 0.5*c` — reproduce exactly.
4. Compare sampler = `MTLCompareFunctionLessEqual` + **Linear** filter; raw sampler = no compare + **Nearest** filter.
5. Depth bias `2.0 / 4.0` on the encoder; front-face `Clockwise`; per-material cull.
6. Depth compare in the shadow PSO = `Less`, depth write on; clear depth = `1.0`.
7. Params `[depthRange, pcss|split, 1/res, 0.02/w]` packed per the Vulkan code; `depthRange=0` disables (shader early-out).
8. Same texel-snapping and cascade z-overlap so the cross-split blend and anti-shimmer behave identically.
9. Shadow pass recorded before the deferred pass in the same command buffer (hazard tracking handles the barrier).
10. Bind the single atlas to fragment texture slots **3 and 4** with the two respective samplers, plus the player camera buffer carrying the four shadow fields.

## spec:tessellation
================================================================================

I now have complete ground truth: the VS produces world-space attributes, the TCS computes per-edge levels from bubble proximity + warp amplification, the TES interpolates and applies relativistic deformation then projects. I have everything needed to write the spec. Let me produce it.

# Metal Tessellation Pipeline Specification — GEMetalDriver

This spec covers porting the Vulkan adaptive relativistic tessellation path (`GEVulkanDrawCall::createPipeline` / `createShadowPipelines`) to native Metal. It defines two feature-gated backends selected on `GEMetalFeatures::m_mesh_shaders`: (A) the universal **compute-kernel + post-tessellation-vertex** path (`drawPatches` with a tessellation-factor buffer), available on all Apple/Mac2 GPUs; and (B) the Metal-3 **object + mesh shader** fast path. Both cover the solid (color/depth-pre-pass) and shadow (depth-only, biased) passes.

---

## 1. Ground truth from the Vulkan path (what must be reproduced exactly)

The relevant Vulkan source: `/Volumes/Macintosh_HD/Users/user950897/Downloads/MinkowskiKart/lib/graphics_engine/src/ge_vulkan_draw_call.cpp`.

**Selection & gating.**
- `getShader` (line 912) routes static geometry to the `<name>_tess` material variant only when `allow_tessellation && m_adaptive_tessellation && device.tessellationShader == VK_TRUE`. Skinned draws of the same variant are drawn *without* tessellation stages (see `set_tess_enabled(false)` at 2235/2273 — the skinning VS emits the fragment layout directly and would not match the TCS inputs).
- `createAllPipelines` (974) and `createShadowPipelines` (1248) both hard-skip tessellation materials when the feature is unsupported (`skip_material`, lines 985-990; `has_tessellation`, 1361-1365). The Metal port keeps the same skip semantics — a device where neither backend is usable simply builds the non-tess variant.

**Patch topology & tessellation state (both passes).**
- `patchControlPoints = 3` — triangular patches (`VkPipelineTessellationStateCreateInfo`, lines 1274-1277 shadow, 1908-1911 solid).
- Topology switches to `VK_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_PATCH_LIST` when tessellation is on (1904-1905 solid, 1407-1409 shadow), else `TRIANGLE_LIST`.
- `frontFace = VK_FRONT_FACE_CLOCKWISE`; cull = `BACK` if `m_backface_culling` else `NONE` (1938-1940 solid, 1410-1411 shadow). The TES declares `layout(triangles, fractional_odd_spacing, cw)` — CW winding must be preserved through the Metal path.

**The tessellation math (must be byte-for-byte behavior-equivalent).**
- VS `spm_tess.vert`: transforms to **world space** (position, normal, tangent, bitangent), passes per-instance velocity + `disable_rel`, and does *not* project. It writes `gl_Position = world_pos` purely for Apple TCS-cull compatibility.
- TCS `ge_tess.tesc`: passes all 11 varyings through, then on invocation 0 computes three per-edge levels via `getTessLevel(pA,pB)`:
  - `getDistanceToEdge(u_relativity_bubble.xyz, pA, pB)` — distance from warp-bubble center to the edge segment.
  - `target_edge = TARGET_EDGE_LENGTH_NEAR(0.1) * max(1, dist/FULL_TESSELLATION_RADIUS(10)) / getWarpAmplification(pA,pB)` — unbounded adaptive falloff (no hard cutoff), clamped to `[1, MAX_TESS_LEVEL=64]`.
  - `getWarpAmplification` reads the relativity beta vector and observer pos; returns `clamp(1/max(1+dot(beta,dir),0.125),1,8)`.
  - `OuterLevel[0..2]` = per-opposite-edge level; `InnerLevel[0]` = max of the three. **Levels depend only on shared edge endpoints + bubble center**, so adjacent patches agree and no cracks appear — this crack-free invariant must survive the port.
- TES `ge_tess.tese`: barycentric-interpolates all varyings, applies `getRelativisticVisualFade` + `applyRelativisticVisualPosition` at the interpolated world position, renormalizes normal/tangent/bitangent, and projects `gl_Position = u_camera.m_projection_view_matrix * deformed_pos`. Fragment output layout matches `spm_layout.vert`.

**Shadow specifics** (`createShadowPipelines`, 1248-1443): same VS+TCS+TES chain but the fragment stage is the depth-only shader; `depthBiasEnable=VK_TRUE, constant=2.0, slope=4.0` (1303-1305); target is the 2×1 cascade atlas render pass; viewport/scissor are dynamic. Cache key includes tesc+tese names and cull mode (1376-1379).

---

## 2. Shared Metal data model (both backends, both passes)

Define these in a new `ge_metal_tessellation.metal` (+ a small ObjC++ manager `ge_metal_tessellation.mm/.hpp` co-located with `ge_metal_driver.mm`). All three existing Metal libraries (`g_3d_msl`, etc.) are compiled from embedded source strings via `newLibraryWithSource:`; follow that convention.

**Patch layout constant.** `constexpr uint kControlPointsPerPatch = 3;` and `MTLTriangleTessellationFactorsHalf` for the factor buffer (Metal's fixed-function triangle tessellator consumes 4×half: `edgeTessellationFactor[3]` + `insideTessellationFactor[1]`, matching `OuterLevel[0..2]` + `InnerLevel[0]`).

**Control-point struct** — the world-space post-VS output that both the compute kernel (path A) and the object shader (path B) produce, and that the post-tessellation-vertex / mesh shader consumes. It mirrors the 11 TCS varyings:

```
struct GEMetalTessControlPoint {
    float4 world_position;   // loc 8
    float4 vertex_color;     // loc 0
    float2 uv;               // loc 1
    float2 uv_two;           // loc 2
    float3 normal;           // loc 5  (world space, un-normalized)
    float3 tangent;          // loc 6
    float3 bitangent;        // loc 7
    float3 velocity;         // loc 9  (per-instance)
    float  hue_change;       // loc 4
    float  disable_rel;      // loc 10
    int    material_id;      // loc 3  (flat)
};
```

**Uniform buffers** reused verbatim from the existing Metal 3D binding scheme: camera UBO (`m_projection_view_matrix`), the relativity bridge uniforms (`u_relativity_bubble`, beta vector, `u_relativity_observer_pos`), the object/instance SSBO, and — for solid — the material/texture bindings. The MSL translations of `relativity_bridge.glsl` / `relativity_visual.vert` / `camera.glsl` already exist in `data/shaders/ge_metal/common` and `shared`; the tessellation kernels `#include` those so the deformation math is single-sourced with the raster paths.

**Vertex fetch.** Both paths pull raw geometry using the existing SPM vertex descriptor (`vd3` in `ge_metal_driver.mm:531`, `S3DVertexSkinnedMesh`, stride 48: pos f3@0, normal Int1010102N@12, color UChar4N@16, uv Half2@20, tangent@28). The per-patch VS logic (`spm_tess.vert`) is reproduced inside the compute kernel (A) / object shader (B) rather than as a separate vertex stage.

---

## 3. Path A — Compute kernel + post-tessellation-vertex (universal)

This is the always-available backend (`m_mesh_shaders == false`, or as the portable default). It maps the Vulkan VS→TCS→TES chain onto Metal's tessellation model: **compute kernel = VS+TCS** (transform + factor computation), **fixed-function tessellator** (replaces the fixed subdivision the TES had implicit), **post-tessellation vertex function = TES** (interpolate + deform + project).

### 3.1 Compute kernel (`ge_tess_kernel`, replaces `spm_tess.vert` + `ge_tess.tesc`)

One threadgroup / one thread per patch (or a threadgroup covering N patches with `[[thread_position_in_grid]]` = patch index). For each patch:
1. Read its 3 control-point indices from the (index buffer, patch) mapping and fetch the 3 raw SPM vertices.
2. Run the `spm_tess.vert` body per control point: object transform → world position/normal/tangent, bitangent = `cross(n,t)*tangent.w`, vertex color `.zyxw` swizzle, uv translation, material-id resolution, velocity/`disable_rel` from the instance. Write the 3 `GEMetalTessControlPoint`s into the **control-point output buffer** at `patch_id*3 + i`.
3. Run the `ge_tess.tesc` factor math: `getTessLevel` for the three opposite edges plus warp amplification; write `MTLTriangleTessellationFactorsHalf{ edge[3]=Outer, inside=max(...) }` into the **factor buffer** at index `patch_id`. Clamp to `[1,64]`. **Critical:** compute edge factors from the *shared, endpoint-only* formula so neighbor patches produce identical half-precision factors — do the level computation in `float` then convert to `half` last, so both sides round identically and stay crack-free.

Dispatch via a `MTLComputeCommandEncoder` before the render encoder (or the same command buffer, ordered). Buffers use `MTLStorageModeShared` (UMA — `m_unified_memory`, so no staging). Both the control-point buffer and the factor buffer are ring-buffered per frame-in-flight.

### 3.2 Render pipeline descriptor (post-tessellation vertex)

On `MTLRenderPipelineDescriptor`:
- `maxTessellationFactor = 64` (matches `MAX_TESS_LEVEL`).
- `tessellationFactorFormat = MTLTessellationFactorFormatHalf`.
- `tessellationPartitionMode = MTLTessellationPartitionModeFractionalOdd` (the TES `fractional_odd_spacing`).
- `tessellationOutputWindingOrder = MTLWindingClockwise` (the TES `cw` + Vulkan `VK_FRONT_FACE_CLOCKWISE`).
- `tessellationControlPointIndexType = MTLTessellationControlPointIndexTypeNone` (control points are laid out contiguously per patch in the kernel-produced buffer; no separate CP index buffer).
- `tessellationFactorStepFunction = MTLTessellationFactorStepFunctionConstant` (one factor set per patch, per-draw).
- `vertexFunction` = the **post-tessellation vertex function** `ge_tess_post_vertex` (see 3.3); `fragmentFunction` = the material's existing Metal fragment function (solid) or the depth-only fragment (shadow).
- `vertexDescriptor`: control points bound as a stage-in buffer with `stepFunction = MTLVertexStepFunctionPerPatchControlPoint` and the `GEMetalTessControlPoint` attribute layout; alternatively bind the CP buffer directly and index by `[[patch]]`/`[[patch_control_point]]` (simpler given the struct is non-vertex-format-friendly — prefer the `patch_control_point<T>` template form).

### 3.3 Post-tessellation vertex function (`ge_tess_post_vertex`, replaces `ge_tess.tese`)

Declared `[[patch(triangle, 3)]]`, taking `float3 tess_coord [[position_in_patch]]` and `patch_control_point<GEMetalTessControlPoint> cp`. Body reproduces `ge_tess.tese`: barycentric interpolate all varyings with `tess_coord.xyz`; `getRelativisticVisualFade` + `applyRelativisticVisualPosition` at interpolated world pos; renormalize normal/tangent/bitangent; output fragment struct matching `spm_layout` MSL; `position = camera.m_projection_view_matrix * deformed_pos`. Velocity/`disable_rel`/material_id taken from control point 0 (per-instance, per the TES).

### 3.4 Draw call

Replace `drawIndexedPrimitives:MTLPrimitiveTypeTriangle` (currently at `ge_metal_driver.mm:306/331`) with, for tess-enabled draws:

```
[enc setRenderPipelineState:tessPipeline];
[enc setTessellationFactorBuffer:factorBuf offset:patchBase*8 instanceStride:0];
[enc setVertexBuffer:cpBuf offset:0 atIndex:kCPBufferIndex];
[enc drawPatches:3
      patchStart:0 patchCount:numPatches
      patchIndexBuffer:nil patchIndexBufferOffset:0
      instanceCount:instances baseInstance:0];
```

`numPatches = indexCount/3`. Set cull mode from the material: `[enc setCullMode: backface ? MTLCullModeBack : MTLCullModeNone]`, `[enc setFrontFacingWinding:MTLWindingClockwise]`. For instanced draws, the kernel must be dispatched per (patch × instance) or the CP buffer sized `patches*instances`; simplest is to fold instancing into the kernel grid and use `instanceCount:1` on the draw. (Vulkan gets instancing free through the pipeline; on Metal the kernel is the natural place to expand instances.)

---

## 4. Path B — Metal-3 object + mesh shaders (`m_mesh_shaders == true`)

Gated on `GEMetalDriver::getMetalFeatures().m_mesh_shaders` (populated in `ge_metal_features.mm:47-51` as `m_apple7_or_newer || m_mac2_family`). This collapses VS+TCS+TES+tessellator into an **object shader** (amplification / factor decision) + **mesh shader** (emit the subdivided micro-mesh), avoiding the fixed-function tessellator round-trip and the intermediate factor/CP buffers.

### 4.1 Pipeline object

Use `MTLMeshRenderPipelineDescriptor` (Metal 3):
- `objectFunction = ge_tess_object`, `meshFunction = ge_tess_mesh`, `fragmentFunction` = material fragment (solid) or depth-only (shadow).
- `objectThreadgroupSizeIsMultipleOfThreadExecutionWidth`, and set `maxTotalThreadgroupsPerMeshGrid` / `payloadMemoryLength` appropriately.
- `colorAttachments[0].pixelFormat` / `depthAttachmentPixelFormat` as in the existing 3D descriptor (`ge_metal_driver.mm:548-549`); for shadow, no color attachment and the shadow depth format, plus depth-bias set on the render encoder.
- Build via `newRenderPipelineStateWithMeshDescriptor:options:reflection:error:`.

### 4.2 Object shader (`ge_tess_object`) — one threadgroup per input patch

- Runs the `spm_tess.vert` transform for the patch's 3 control points and the `ge_tess.tesc` factor math (same `getTessLevel` / `getWarpAmplification`, identical clamps).
- Converts the fractional-odd factors into an **integer subdivision count** for the mesh grid: derive `segments = ceil(max_outer)` (clamped 1..64), and pass the *fractional* edge/inside factors plus the 3 world-space control points (the full `GEMetalTessControlPoint` triple) into the object→mesh **payload** (`object_data ... [[payload]]`).
- Emits the mesh grid size: `mesh_grid_properties.set_threadgroups_per_grid(uint3(tilesX, tilesY, 1))` sized to cover the subdivided triangle count. **Crack-free requirement:** compute per-edge segment counts from the shared endpoint-only formula (not from the inside factor), so a shared edge is subdivided identically from both adjacent patches. Snapping to integer segments must use the same rounding on both sides — round the *edge* factor, keyed on sorted endpoint identity, exactly as the level formula already guarantees agreement.

### 4.3 Mesh shader (`ge_tess_mesh`) — emits the micro-mesh

- Reads the payload. Generates the barycentric coordinates for the subdivided triangle grid matching `fractional_odd_spacing` (with the reduced-density boundary rings so the outer-edge segment count matches neighbors — this is the mesh-shader equivalent of the fixed tessellator honoring outer vs inside levels).
- Per generated vertex: run the `ge_tess.tese` body (interpolate, `applyRelativisticVisualPosition`, renormalize, project). Emit into `mesh` vertices; emit indices in **CW** winding.
- Emit per-primitive material_id if needed for the fragment stage (flat).
- Cap: `set_primitive_count(...)` per threadgroup; if a single patch's subdivision exceeds one mesh threadgroup's max (Metal caps ~256 vertices / ~256 primitives per mesh threadgroup), the object shader must fan out to multiple mesh threadgroups (raise `tilesX/tilesY`) and each mesh threadgroup renders a sub-tile of the patch. Level-64 triangular patches can exceed the per-threadgroup limit, so tiling is mandatory, not optional.

### 4.4 Draw call

```
[enc setRenderPipelineState:meshTessPipeline];
[enc setObjectBuffer:cameraUBO offset:0 atIndex:...];  // + relativity, object SSBO, material buffers
[enc drawMeshThreadgroups:MTLSizeMake(numPatches*instances,1,1)
   threadsPerObjectThreadgroup:MTLSizeMake(3,1,1)     // 3 CPs per patch
   threadsPerMeshThreadgroup:MTLSizeMake(kMeshTGWidth,1,1)];
```

No factor buffer, no CP buffer, no pre-pass compute dispatch — the object stage subsumes both. Cull/winding set on the encoder as in Path A.

---

## 5. Solid vs shadow — the two pass variants (applies to both backends)

The two paths differ only in fragment stage + render-target/raster state; the object/kernel/mesh geometry stages are shared (same VS+TCS+TES logic). Build **one tessellation pipeline object per (material, pass)** exactly as the Vulkan code builds per-material solid and shadow pipelines.

**Solid (color + depth-pre-pass).**
- Fragment function = the material's existing Metal 3D fragment (from the `_tess` material's base shader — the tess variant reuses the base material's fragment/depth-only fragment; see `ge_material_manager.cpp:256-258` where only VS/tesc/tese are overridden).
- Depth state: for the color pass after a depth pre-pass, `depthCompareFunction = MTLCompareFunctionEqual`, `depthWriteEnabled = NO` (mirrors `VK_COMPARE_OP_EQUAL` + no depth write at `ge_vulkan_draw_call.cpp:2250-2252`). For the pre-pass itself, `Less` + write, depth-only fragment.
- Color attachment(s) match the deferred G-buffer count when the deferred FBO is active (the Vulkan code resizes `color_blend_attachment` per pass, 1979-2009); the Metal descriptor sets the corresponding `colorAttachments[i].pixelFormat` for each G-buffer target.
- Cull = material `m_backface_culling`, winding CW.

**Shadow (depth-only, biased).**
- No color attachment; `depthAttachmentPixelFormat` = shadow map depth format; render target = the 2×1 cascade atlas.
- Fragment function = depth-only Metal fragment (or nil where alpha-test isn't needed).
- Depth bias applied on the render command encoder, not the pipeline: `[enc setDepthBias:2.0f slopeScale:4.0f clamp:0.0f]` (equals Vulkan `constant=2.0, slope=4.0` at 1304-1305). Depth state `Less` + write.
- Viewport/scissor set dynamically per cascade (Vulkan uses dynamic viewport/scissor, 1327-1336).
- Cull from material; winding CW.
- **Skinned exception preserved:** for skinned draws of a `_tess` material, both passes fall back to the non-tessellated skinning pipeline (no object/kernel/mesh stage) — mirror `set_tess_enabled(false)` / the shadow `use_tess = has_tessellation && !skinning` rule (1375). The skinning VS emits the fragment layout directly.

---

## 6. Pipeline caching & selection

- Cache key must include: material shader name, pass (solid-color / depth-pre / shadow), backend (compute-tess vs mesh-tess), cull mode, and — for shadow — the bias-carrying variant. This mirrors the Vulkan cache keys (`dp_cache_key` at 2139-2152 and the shadow `key` at 1376-1379), which already fold tesc+tese names + `|cull`/`|nocull`.
- Backend choice is made once at pipeline-build time from `m_mesh_shaders`; store the chosen enum on the pipeline record so the draw loop knows whether to emit a compute dispatch + `drawPatches` (A) or `drawMeshThreadgroups` (B).
- Feature-skip: if neither backend is usable (should not happen since Path A works on all Apple/Mac2 GPUs, but guard anyway), fall back to the non-tess material — identical to the Vulkan `skip_material` behavior (985-990). The `_tess` selection in the Metal analog of `getShader` must additionally require the runtime tessellation capability, matching lines 941-949.

---

## 7. Correctness invariants to verify

1. **No cracks.** Both backends must derive per-edge subdivision from the endpoint-only, bubble-relative formula, and convert to half / integer *identically* on both sides of every shared edge. This is the single highest-risk item — the fixed-function tessellator (A) gets this for free from the half-factor buffer; the mesh path (B) must snap edge segment counts deterministically.
2. **Winding.** CW throughout (kernel/tessellator output winding = `MTLWindingClockwise`; mesh emits CW; encoder `setFrontFacingWinding:MTLWindingClockwise`). Regression here inverts back-face culling versus the existing Metal 3D path (which already matches `VK_FRONT_FACE_CLOCKWISE`, per commit `a4dcc2f`).
3. **Deformation single-sourcing.** The post-tess vertex / mesh shader must call the *same* `applyRelativisticVisualPosition` / `getRelativisticVisualFade` MSL used by the non-tess raster path, so tessellated and non-tessellated geometry warp identically at patch boundaries where levels collapse to 1.
4. **Level-1 identity.** A patch clamped to tess level 1 (distant geometry) must produce exactly the original triangle, so the transition between tess and non-tess draws is seamless.
5. **Shadow bias parity.** `2.0` constant / `4.0` slope on the encoder — visually validate against acne on large tessellated ground planes.

---

---

# Spec: Wiring the `data/shaders/ge_metal/` MSL tree into the native Metal backend

## 0. Current state (what exists, what is missing)

The pieces are present but disconnected:

- **The MSL tree** (`data/shaders/ge_metal/`) is a faithful port of `ge_shaders/` (57 files), guarded by the *same* preprocessor macros the Vulkan path uses (`PBR_ENABLED`, `BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE`, `SAMPLER_SIZE`, `TOTAL_MESH_TEXTURE_LAYER`, `GE_SAMPLE_TEX_INDEX`, `TILED_GPU`, `GE_DISABLE_DISPLACE_SSR`) plus MSL-only `[[function_constant(n)]]` specialization constants.
- **`ge_metal_shader_manager.mm`** is a runtime MSL compiler: it inlines `#include "..."` by hand (MSL runtime `newLibraryWithSource:` has no include search path), prepends a predefine block, calls `newLibraryWithSource:`, caches `MTLLibrary` per file and `MTLFunction` per `(file, function, bool-constant-set)`, and specializes via `MTLFunctionConstantValues` (bool only).
- **`ge_metal_features.mm`** already detects `m_argument_buffers_tier` (Tier2 → `m_bindless`), Apple7+, unified memory, RW-texture tier, sampler cap 16.

The gaps this spec closes:

1. **The shader manager is orphaned.** `GEMetalShaderManager::init()` is never called from `ge_metal_driver.mm`, and `getShaderFolder()` returns `.../ge_shaders/` (the GLSL folder), never `.../ge_metal/`. The driver today hand-compiles three inline MSL string literals (`g_2d_msl`, `g_3d_msl`, `g_3ds_msl`) at `ge_metal_driver.mm:493-591` and pulls functions by literal name (`ge2d_vertex`, etc.). Nothing in the driver ever touches the `ge_metal/` tree.
2. **Predefine parity is incomplete.** `init()` injects `PBR_ENABLED / SAMPLER_SIZE / TOTAL_MESH_TEXTURE_LAYER / TILED_GPU / GE_DISABLE_DISPLACE_SSR` but *not* the bindless macros (`BIND_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE`, `BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE`) nor `GE_SAMPLE_TEX_INDEX` — yet every material shader `#ifdef`s on them. The `if (const GEMetalDriver* d = getMTLDriver())` block at lines 104-107 is a stub that discards `d`.
3. **Function constants are bool-only.** `getFunction` handles `MTLDataTypeBool`, but `shared/ge_metal_bindings.h` declares `float u_specular_levels_minus_one [[function_constant(1)]]` and `uint u_hiz_iterations [[function_constant(5)]]`. Any pipeline that specializes those cannot be built through the current API.
4. **No argument-buffer material binding.** `sample_mesh_texture.h` and `solid.metal` expect a `constant GEMeshTextures&` argument buffer at `GE_MTL_BUF_MESH_TEXTURES`, but no code builds an `MTLArgumentEncoder` or binds it.
5. **Two conflicting binding headers.** `common/ge_metal_bindings.h` and `shared/ge_metal_bindings.h` both use guard `GE_METAL_BINDINGS_H` and assign *different* indices (e.g. mesh-texture argument buffer is `buffer 10` in common/ vs `buffer 7` in shared/; push constants `buffer 8` vs `buffer 15`; IBL/AO/shadow slots differ). Whichever is `#include`d first wins and silently poisons the other. This must be unified before anything downstream is reliable.
6. **No offline compile / pipeline cache.** Everything is runtime `newLibraryWithSource:` — no `.metallib`, no `MTLBinaryArchive`. First-frame hitching and per-launch recompilation are unaddressed.

The rest of this spec defines the target design for each of these.

---

## 1. Unify the binding header (prerequisite, do this first)

`common/ge_metal_bindings.h` and `shared/ge_metal_bindings.h` are mutually incompatible and share an include guard, so they can never both be in one translation unit and produce different layouts depending on include order. Collapse to **one canonical header**, `data/shaders/ge_metal/common/ge_metal_bindings.h`, and delete `shared/ge_metal_bindings.h` (update the four `shared/*.h` includers — `handle_pbr.h`, `pbr_light.h`, `pbr_utils.h`, `relativity_bridge.h` — to point at `../common/ge_metal_bindings.h`).

The canonical header is the single source of truth for three families of constants, and its numbering is mirrored on the C++ side by an enum (see §3):

- **Buffer slots** `GE_MTL_BUF_*` — `CAMERA=0, OBJECT=1, SKINNING=2, GLOBAL_LIGHT=3, MATERIAL_IDS=4, SHADOW_NEAR=5, SHADOW_FAR=6`. Reserve **7** for the mesh-texture argument buffer (`GE_MTL_BUF_MESH_TEXTURES`) — the `shared/` value — because argument buffers must live above the engine SSBOs and below the vertex stream. Push constants go to a **fixed high slot 15** (`GE_MTL_BUF_PUSH_CONSTANT`), matching `shared/`, so the CPU can offset the `[[stage_in]]` vertex buffer to any slot `≥16` without collision. (The `common/` values of `PUSH=8` / `MESH_TEXTURES=10` are dropped.)
- **Texture slots** `GE_MTL_TEX_*` — mesh fallback `MESH0=0 .. +7`, `AO=... `, `IBL_DIFFUSE / IBL_SPECULAR`, `SUN_SHADOW_PCF / SUN_SHADOW_RAW`. Pick one contiguous, non-overlapping assignment (the `common/` file already documents the sun-shadow-at-16/17 rationale; keep that and slot AO/IBL so the fallback mesh range `0..7`, AO/IBL, and shadow range `16+` never collide).
- **Sampler slots** `GE_MTL_SAMP_*` — Metal binds a texture and its sampler independently; keep the convention that a texture at index *N* pairs with a sampler at index *N* (as `solid.metal` already assumes: `[[texture(GE_MTL_TEX_MESH0)]]` + `[[sampler(GE_MTL_TEX_MESH0)]]`).
- **Function constants** — keep the `constant … [[function_constant(n)]]` declarations (`u_ibl=0, u_specular_levels_minus_one=1, u_deferred=2, u_has_skybox=3, u_ssr=4, u_hiz_iterations=5`) in this one header. These indices are the contract with `getFunction` (§4).

This header is pure MSL (`metal::float4x4` etc.) and is offline-compiled; the C++ side never `#include`s it. Instead a **generated companion** `ge_metal_binding_indices.h` (plain C++ `enum`) is emitted from the same numbers so the driver and the MSL cannot drift (see §3).

---

## 2. Predefine / function-constant injection

Two distinct specialization mechanisms exist and must be kept separate, mirroring how the Vulkan path uses shaderc `#define`s vs SPIR-V spec-constants:

### 2a. Preprocessor predefines (compile-time, per library)

`GEMetalShaderManager::init()` builds `g_predefines` once and prepends it to every source before `newLibraryWithSource:`. It must reach **full parity** with `GEVulkanShaderManager::loadAllShaders` (`ge_vulkan_shader_manager.cpp:84-119`), translated to Metal semantics:

| GLSL predefine | Metal predefine | Source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| `#version 450` | *(omit — MSL has no `#version`; set `opts.languageVersion` instead, §5)* | — |
| `PBR_ENABLED 1` (+ `g_mesh_texture_layer=8`) | same | `getGEConfig()->m_pbr` |
| `SAMPLER_SIZE`, `TOTAL_MESH_TEXTURE_LAYER` | same | `g_sampler_size`, layer count |
| `BIND_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE` | same, **iff** device is bindless | `features.m_bindless` |
| `BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE` | same, **iff** device is bindless (Tier2) | `features.m_bindless` |
| `GE_SAMPLE_TEX_INDEX nonuniformEXT` / `int` | **always `int`** (MSL argument-buffer indexing is inherently divergence-tolerant; the header comment in `sample_mesh_texture.h` already states this) | constant |
| `SHADER_STORAGE_IMAGE_EXTENDED_FORMATS` | same, iff `features.m_read_write_texture_tier >= 2` | RW tier |
| `TILED_GPU`, `GE_DISABLE_DISPLACE_SSR` | already emitted unconditionally (correct — Metal is always tile-based) | constant |

Concretely, `init()` must be extended to take the resolved `GEMetalFeatures` (see §3) and replace the dead `if (const GEMetalDriver* d = getMTLDriver())` stub with:

```
if (features.m_bindless) {
    oss << "#define BIND_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE 1\n";
    oss << "#define BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE 1\n";
}
oss << "#define GE_SAMPLE_TEX_INDEX int\n";
if (features.m_read_write_texture_tier >= 2)
    oss << "#define SHADER_STORAGE_IMAGE_EXTENDED_FORMATS 1\n";
```

Because the predefine set changes the *layout* of `GEMeshTextures` (its array is `SAMPLER_SIZE * TOTAL_MESH_TEXTURE_LAYER`) and whether the bindless path is even taken, `g_predefines` is part of the **cache key** for any offline artifact (§5): a `.metallib` built for `PBR_ENABLED=1, bindless` is not interchangeable with one built for the fallback path.

### 2b. Function constants (link-time, per pipeline variant)

Predefines are baked per-`MTLLibrary`; the remaining per-*pipeline* switches are the `[[function_constant(n)]]` values, resolved when a specific `MTLFunction` is pulled. This is the direct analog of SPIR-V `layout(constant_id=n)` spec-constants and is the mechanism the material system should use for anything that varies per draw-batch *without* recompiling the whole library — `u_deferred`, `u_ibl`, `u_has_skybox`, `u_ssr` (bool), and `u_specular_levels_minus_one` (float), `u_hiz_iterations` (uint).

The current `getFunction` only accepts `std::map<unsigned,bool>`. Generalize it to carry typed values:

```
struct GEMTLFunctionConstant {
    enum { Bool, Float, Uint } m_type;
    union { bool b; float f; uint32_t u; } m_value;
};
void* getFunction(const std::string& file, const std::string& func,
                  const std::map<unsigned, GEMTLFunctionConstant>& constants = {});
```

The setter loop chooses `MTLDataTypeBool / MTLDataTypeFloat / MTLDataTypeUInt` and `setConstantValue:type:atIndex:` accordingly. The cache key string already folds constant index+value (`file|func|idx=val|...`) — extend it to encode the typed value so a `float` variant never aliases a `bool` variant. Keep the existing bool-only overload as a thin wrapper for call-site compatibility.

Rationale for the split: predefines change resource *shapes* (struct sizes, which parameters exist) and therefore the whole library and its offline artifact; function constants change *scalar behaviour inside one library* and are cheap to re-specialize at pipeline-build time, so they belong on the per-pipeline key, not the per-library key.

---

## 3. Wiring the manager into the driver

Today `GEMetalShaderManager::init` is dead code. The driver must:

1. **Add a Metal shader folder accessor.** `ge_main.cpp` only exposes `getShaderFolder()` → `…/ge_shaders/`. Add `getMetalShaderFolder()` → `…/ge_metal/` (set alongside `setShaderFolder`), and have the driver pass it into `GEMetalShaderManager::init`.
2. **Call `init` right after feature detection.** In `GEMetalDriver` construction, immediately after `geMetalPopulateFeatures(...)` at `ge_metal_driver.mm:448`, call `GEMetalShaderManager::init(this, (__bridge void*)m_impl->device, getMetalShaderFolder())`, passing the populated `m_impl->features` so §2a can consult `m_bindless` / RW-tier. Change the `init` signature to accept `const GEMetalFeatures&` (or read it back through the `GEMetalDriver*` it already receives — the driver stores `m_impl->features`; expose a `const GEMetalFeatures& getFeatures() const` on `GEMetalDriver` and have `init` call it, which also lets §2a stop hard-coding).
3. **Retire the inline MSL literals.** Replace the three hand-written `newLibraryWithSource:` blocks (`ge_metal_driver.mm:461-591`) with `GEMetalShaderManager::getFunction(file, entry, constants)`. The 2D/3D/std-3D pipelines become entries in the tree (e.g. `2d_render.metal` already exists with the right functions; the 3D forward pipeline maps onto `solid.metal` / `spm.metal`). The `MTLVertexDescriptor` construction stays in the driver (it is CPU-side layout, not shader source), but `pd.vertexFunction`/`fragmentFunction` are filled from the manager.
4. **Emit the C++ binding-index companion.** Add a generated header `ge_metal_binding_indices.h` (an `enum` copy of the `GE_MTL_BUF_* / TEX_* / SAMP_*` numbers from §1) so `setFragmentBuffer:offset:atIndex:` / `setVertexBuffer:` / `setFragmentTexture:atIndex:` call sites use the same symbolic indices as the MSL. Generation options, cheapest first: (a) a tiny CMake `configure_file`/script that greps the `#define`s out of the MSL header into an `enum`; (b) hand-maintain with a `static_assert`-style comment cross-reference. Option (a) is preferred so the two can never drift.

---

## 4. Argument-buffer material binding

The material path (`solid.metal`, `alphatest.metal`, `transparent.metal`, `normalmap.metal`, `splatting.metal`, `spm*.metal`, `grass.metal`, …) expects, on a Tier2 device, the entire mesh-texture table as **one argument buffer** `GEMeshTextures` at `GE_MTL_BUF_MESH_TEXTURES`, plus a single shared `sampler` — exactly the GLSL `BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE` bindless array. Design:

1. **Build the encoder from the function, not by hand.** After pulling the fragment `MTLFunction`, create `id<MTLArgumentEncoder> enc = [fn newArgumentEncoderWithBufferIndex:GE_MTL_BUF_MESH_TEXTURES]`. This makes Metal compute the `[[id(n)]]` layout of `GEMeshTextures` (an `array<texture2d<float>, SAMPLER_SIZE*TOTAL_MESH_TEXTURE_LAYER>`) instead of the driver guessing offsets. Allocate one backing `MTLBuffer` of `enc.encodedLength` with `MTLStorageModeShared` (UMA — no staging).
2. **Populate on texture-table change, not per draw.** The mesh-texture descriptor set is rebuilt when the material set changes (mirroring `GEVulkanTextureDescriptor`). At that point, `[enc setArgumentBuffer:buf offset:0]` then `[enc setTexture:mtlTex atIndex:i]` for each of the `TOTAL_MESH_TEXTURE_LAYER * material_count` slots. Empty slots point at a 1×1 fallback texture so indexing `t.f_mesh_textures[id]` is always valid (matching how the GLSL array is fully populated). This exactly reproduces the index math `TOTAL_MESH_TEXTURE_LAYER * material_id + layer` that `sample_mesh_texture.h` bakes in.
3. **Residency.** Argument-buffer textures are not automatically resident. Before each encoder that binds the argument buffer, call `[renderEncoder useResource:tex usage:MTLResourceUsageRead stages:MTLRenderStageFragment]` for every referenced texture — or, more cheaply, drive a single `id<MTLHeap>` that all mesh textures are sub-allocated from and call `useHeap:` once. The heap approach is strongly preferred at 512×layer textures; make it the design target and note `useResource:` as the correctness-first fallback.
4. **Bind at draw time.** `[enc'... setFragmentBuffer:argBuf offset:0 atIndex:GE_MTL_BUF_MESH_TEXTURES]` (the render encoder) plus `setFragmentSamplerState:mesh_sampler atIndex:GE_MTL_TEX_MESH0`. The single shared sampler matches `solid.metal`'s `sampler mesh_sampler [[sampler(GE_MTL_TEX_MESH0)]]`.
5. **Fallback path (Tier1 / non-bindless).** When `BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE` is *not* defined, `solid.metal` takes individual `texture2d` + `sampler` parameters at `GE_MTL_TEX_MESH0 + {0,2}`. Here the driver binds up to 8 textures/samplers per stage directly with `setFragmentTexture:atIndex:` / `setFragmentSamplerState:atIndex:`, respecting the 16-sampler cap (`features.m_max_samplers_per_stage`). This is why the predefine in §2a is gated on `m_bindless` — the two code paths must agree at compile time.

The engine UBO/SSBO block (camera/object/skinning/light/material-ids at buffers 0–4, shadow at 5–6) is *not* an argument buffer; those are bound as plain `setVertexBuffer:`/`setFragmentBuffer:` at their `GE_MTL_BUF_*` indices, exactly as the shared struct layouts in the binding header specify.

---

## 5. Offline `.metal → .metallib` CMake step + `MTLBinaryArchive` pipeline cache

Two independent caches, at two stages of the pipeline. Both are opt-in accelerators with a runtime fallback (§6), never a hard dependency.

### 5a. Offline library compile (source → AIR → metallib) via the Xcode Metal Toolchain

Goal: ship a prebuilt `default.metallib` per predefine-variant so the app skips `newLibraryWithSource:` (and the hand-rolled `#include` inliner) entirely on machines where the toolchain-built artifact matches.

- **Tooling.** Use `xcrun -sdk macosx metal` and `xcrun -sdk macosx metallib` (Xcode Metal Toolchain). Unlike the runtime source compiler, the offline `metal` front-end **has a real include search path**, so pass `-I data/shaders/ge_metal` and the hand-inlining of `#include` becomes unnecessary for the offline path (the runtime inliner stays only for the fallback).
- **CMake structure.** Add a `METAL_PRECOMPILE` option (default `ON` when `METAL_NATIVE AND APPLE`), guarded so non-Apple / cross builds skip it. For each top-level `*.metal` entry point file:
  - `add_custom_command` running `xcrun -sdk macosx metal -c <file> -o <file>.air` with:
    - `-I ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/data/shaders/ge_metal` and `-I .../ge_metal/common`,
    - the **predefine flags as real `-D` flags** (`-DPBR_ENABLED=1 -DSAMPLER_SIZE=512 -DTOTAL_MESH_TEXTURE_LAYER=8 -DBIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE=1 -DTILED_GPU=1 -DGE_DISABLE_DISPLACE_SSR=1 -DGE_SAMPLE_TEX_INDEX=int`) — the same block §2a would emit at runtime, so offline and runtime produce identical AIR,
    - `-std=metal3.0` (or the minimum the tree needs) matching the runtime `opts.languageVersion`,
    - `-frecord-sources` (embeds source for GPU-frame-capture debugging) in Debug builds only.
  - **Variant matrix.** Because bindless vs fallback and PBR vs non-PBR change struct shapes, the precompile emits a small matrix of metallibs, named by predefine hash, e.g. `ge_metal_pbr_bindless.metallib`, `ge_metal_pbr_fallback.metallib`, `ge_metal_nopbr_*.metallib`. The runtime picks the file whose predefine set matches the resolved `g_predefines` (which itself is derived from `m_pbr` + `m_bindless` + RW-tier).
  - `add_custom_command` running `xcrun -sdk macosx metallib <all .air for that variant> -o ge_metal_<variant>.metallib`, with an `add_custom_target(ge_metallibs ALL DEPENDS …)` so it builds with the app, and an `install(FILES …)`/copy into the runtime shader directory next to `ge_metal/`.
- **Dependency tracking.** List every `common/*.h` and `shared/*.h` as `DEPENDS` (or use `metal -MMD` to emit `.d` depfiles consumed via `DEPFILE`) so editing a shared header reliably rebuilds the affected metallibs. This mirrors how `STK_SHADERS`/`stkshaders` are tracked today (`CMakeLists.txt:903`).
- **Runtime load.** Add `GEMetalShaderManager::loadPrecompiledLibrary()` that resolves the variant filename from `g_predefines`, loads it via `[device newLibraryWithURL:… error:]`, and if it succeeds routes `getLibrary()` to return this single archived library (functions are pulled by name from it, identical to the source-compiled case). Store the metallib’s embedded hash/version and compare against the expected predefine hash; a mismatch (e.g. shipped metallib is stale vs the running config) falls through to source compile (§6).

### 5b. `MTLBinaryArchive` pipeline-state cache (metallib → compiled PSO)

Even with a prebuilt metallib, `newRenderPipelineStateWithDescriptor:` still JITs the GPU-specific pipeline on first use (front-end AIR → back-end ISA for *this* GPU) — that is the real first-frame hitch. `MTLBinaryArchive` caches the *back-end* result, keyed by the full `MTLRenderPipelineDescriptor` (functions + function-constants + vertex descriptor + attachment formats).

- **Location.** GPU-ISA is device- and driver-version specific, so this cache is written to a **user-writable app-support path** at runtime (not shipped in the bundle): e.g. `~/Library/Application Support/…/metal_pso_cache_<deviceName>_<osBuild>.bin`.
- **Populate.** Create `id<MTLBinaryArchive> archive = [device newBinaryArchiveWithDescriptor:desc error:]` (loading from the cache URL if present). Before building each PSO, `[archive addRenderPipelineFunctionsWithDescriptor:pd error:]`; set `pd.binaryArchives = @[archive]` so `newRenderPipelineStateWithDescriptor:` reads the compiled variant out of the archive instead of recompiling. After the frame’s pipelines are built (or on clean shutdown), `[archive serializeToURL:cacheURL error:]`.
- **Warm-up.** Optionally, precreate the known pipeline permutations (2D, 3D-SPM, 3D-std, skybox, alphatest, transparent, depth-only, the GTAO/HiZ/IBL compute passes) at load into the archive so the first real draw of each is a cache hit. This is the Metal analog of a pipeline-cache pre-warm.
- **Invalidation.** Key the cache filename on device name + OS build + a content hash of the metallib(s). Any change to the GPU, OS, or shaders yields a new filename; the stale file is simply ignored/GC’d. A corrupt/incompatible archive must be caught (the `newBinaryArchiveWithDescriptor:` / `addRenderPipelineFunctions…` error) and treated as a cold cache, never fatal.

The two caches compose: `.metallib` removes source compilation, `MTLBinaryArchive` removes PSO recompilation. Each is independently skippable.

---

## 6. Runtime fallback (correctness-first, four-level ladder)

The offline artifacts are optimizations. The system degrades cleanly, in this priority order, and every downgrade is logged once via `os::Printer::log("GEMetalShaderManager", …)` (as the existing error paths already do):

1. **Prebuilt metallib + valid binary archive** (fast path). Predefine-variant metallib loads, `MTLBinaryArchive` hits → no compilation at all.
2. **Prebuilt metallib, cold/failed archive.** Metallib loads but the PSO isn’t in the archive (first run on this GPU/OS, or archive rejected). Build PSOs via `newRenderPipelineStateWithDescriptor:` normally and repopulate the archive for next launch.
3. **No usable metallib → runtime source compile** (the *current* code path). `loadPrecompiledLibrary()` fails (file missing, predefine-hash mismatch, `newLibraryWithURL:` error, or `METAL_PRECOMPILE=OFF`) → fall back to `getLibrary()`’s existing `inlineIncludes` + `g_predefines` + `newLibraryWithSource:`. This must remain fully functional and is the guaranteed baseline — it is what ships if the Xcode Metal Toolchain is unavailable at build time (CI without full Xcode) or the metallib is stale.
4. **Bindless → 16-sampler fallback** (orthogonal, resource-model axis). Independently of how the library was obtained, if `features.m_bindless` is false the predefines omit `BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE`, and §4’s per-texture binding path is used instead of the argument buffer. This is the Metal counterpart of the existing `TILED_GPU` / MoltenVK ≤16-sampler accommodation and must be exercised on Tier1 hardware.

Failure of any single shader compile/pipeline build is non-fatal to the whole backend where possible: log, return `nullptr`/skip that material (matching how `getLibrary`/`getFunction` already return `nullptr` on error), and let the driver fall back to a null/placeholder pipeline for just that draw, so one bad shader doesn’t black-screen the game.

---

**Key correctness invariants to preserve throughout:** offline `-D` flags must byte-for-byte match the runtime `g_predefines` block (so AIR is identical across paths); the C++ `GE_MTL_*` enum must be generated from the one MSL binding header (no drift); the bindless predefine, the `GEMeshTextures` argument-encoder layout, and the 16-sampler fallback must all agree on a single `features.m_bindless` decision; and every cache (metallib variant, binary archive) must be keyed on the full config so a stale artifact is detected and bypassed rather than used.

## Correctness concerns to verify on GPU
================================================================================

- - Could not compile offline: the Xcode Metal toolchain component is not installed on this host (xcrun metal reports 'missing Metal Toolchain'). Verified only by manual review + include-path resolution. Real gate is a runtime newLibraryWithSource: compile in ge_metal_shader_manager.
- - GL->Metal z remap: GLSL does gl_Position = m_projection_view_matrix * pos with GL [-1,1] clip-z. I applied clip.z = (clip.z + clip.w) * 0.5 to match the [0,1] Metal NDC convention that the existing native 3D path (ge3d_vertex) already uses. If the CPU instead bakes the z-remap into m_projection_view_matrix (as some pipelines do), this double-remaps z. Must confirm which convention the Metal camera UBO upload uses before trusting depth.
- - BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE material-id fallback (GLSL: if f_material_id < 0 -> u_material_ids.m_material_id[gl_DrawIDARB]) is omitted. Metal has no direct per-draw gl_DrawIDARB equivalent in a plain vertex fn; the bindless path needs the CPU to pass a base-instance/draw-id or bind per-draw material ids. Documented in-file; wire up when the bindless mesh-texture path is enabled.
- - ObjectData std140 byte layout (packed_float3 + trailing scalar packing, 96-byte total) is load-bearing since the same SSBO feeds both backends; needs a runtime struct-size/offset check against the CPU-side ObjectData writer.
- - CameraBuffer (from relativity_bridge.h) is used for binding buffer(0), which the relativity helpers require; ge_metal_bindings.h also defines a separate GECameraBuffer type. Both must describe the identical byte layout of the uploaded camera UBO. They are field-compatible through the relativity tail, but the two struct definitions should eventually be reconciled to one to avoid drift.
- - VertexIn declares all 8 SPM attributes (pos/normal/color/uv/uv_two/tangent/joint/weight), but the current driver vertex descriptor (ge_metal_driver.mm) only configures attributes 0-3 for the SPM layout. The CPU must extend the MTLVertexDescriptor to cover attributes 4-7 (uv_two Half2@24, tangent Int1010102@28, joint Short4@32, weight Half4@40, stride 48) before these entry points can be used, or Metal will fail to link stage_in.
- - Overlaps with a sibling deliverable: data/shaders/ge_metal/spm.metal already contains a complete port of the SAME spm_skinning.vert as `ge_spm_skinning_vertex` (plus non-skinned and fullscreen variants). Both files can coexist since the Metal shader manager compiles each into a separate MTLLibrary (no duplicate-symbol clash), but the CPU pipeline setup should decide which entry point/file it actually binds. My function is named `spm_skinning_vertex` (in spm_skinning.metal); the sibling's is `ge_spm_skinning_vertex` (in spm.metal).
- - PBR-output interface divergence from the sibling. I guarded f_normal/f_tangent/f_bitangent (and their compute) behind #ifdef PBR_ENABLED to match the GLSL main() body literally; the sibling spm.metal declares and writes them unconditionally. spm_layout.vert always DECLARES these outs (locations 5-7) but only writes them under PBR_ENABLED. If the paired fragment shader's stage_in struct always declares these inputs, my guarded VOut would drop them when PBR is off and cause a vertex/fragment interface mismatch. The two files should agree on this convention; the sibling's always-emit approach is the safer one for interface consistency.
- - BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE bindless material-id fallback uses [[draw_id]] for gl_DrawIDARB. The Metal shader manager does not currently emit BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE, so this path is dead until the CPU side defines it and binds a MaterialIDs SSBO at GE_MTL_BUF_MATERIAL_ID (4). [[draw_id]] equivalence to gl_DrawIDARB across a multi-draw needs GPU verification when that path is enabled.
- - No offline compile was possible (no Metal toolchain on this host; MSL is compiled at runtime via newLibraryWithSource:). Verified by manual review only. Needs a runtime compile + visual check of a skinned character in an AI race. The ObjectData std140 layout (packed_float3 + trailing scalar) was cross-checked field-by-field against C++ GE::ObjectData in ge_vulkan_draw_call.hpp (96-byte stride) and matches, but a byte-offset sanity check against the live SSBO upload is still warranted since the same buffer feeds both backends.
- - Include-guard collision: shared/ge_metal_bindings.h and common/ge_metal_bindings.h both use guard GE_METAL_BINDINGS_H but are NOT identical (different constant names/values, and only the shared one defines GECameraBuffer/GEGlobalLightBuffer/the u_* function-constants/GE_MTL_TEX_MESH0/IBL slots). The port relies on including shared/ge_metal_bindings.h FIRST so the common one is guarded out; this is correct only because of include order. The two headers should be reconciled (sibling-task issue), otherwise any TU that includes common's first would break this file's symbol references.
- - The shader manager (ge_metal_shader_manager.mm init) does NOT emit BIND_MESH_TEXTURES_AT_ONCE or GE_SAMPLE_TEX_INDEX predefines today, so the compiled path is the <=16-sampler fallback (f_mesh_texture_0 at tex/sampler 0, f_mesh_texture_2 at tex/sampler 2). The bindless branch is present but dormant until the CPU adds that define + the argument buffer at GE_MTL_BUF_MESH_TEXTURES.
- - Entry point is named solid_main and its parameter list defines the binding contract the GEMetalDriver must adopt (mesh tex/sampler at GE_MTL_TEX_MESH0 slots; PBR path also needs camera@buffer0, global light@buffer3, IBL diffuse/specular cubes+samplers at tex/sampler 8/9). The current driver still uses inline embedded shader strings and only binds vbuf@0+MVP@1+tex@0, so this pass is not wired end-to-end yet.
- - In the forward (non-deferred) PBR branch o_normal is declared in FragOut but left unwritten, mirroring the GLSL which only writes o_normal in the deferred branch.
